newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas firms late, fronts hit new highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas firms late, fronts hit new highs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures reversed a soft open and headed higher late Tuesday in active trade, with front months driven to new highs by more technical buying and short covering when downside momentum stalled early.

At 1410 EDT, September was up 2.6 cents at $2.40 per million British thermal units after hitting a new contract high of $2.42. October, which also set a new benchmark of $2.42 today, was 3.7 cents higher at $2.405. Most other deferreds were steady to up 3.7 cents.

"The fundamentals may not totally justify these levels, but there is some good load in California and we triggered more (buy) stops above $2.38. Too many people are fighting it, so we could see more upside," said one Southwest trader.
With cash firming today to close the gap to paper and the technical picture still positive, many agreed further upside was in the cards near-term.
But skeptics said the lack of extreme heat in most regions and competitive fuel oil prices should eventually take a toll on demand, particularly if storage rebounds this week.
Injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA inventory report range from 64 bcf to 94 bcf versus a gain last year of 84 bcf.
Mostly normal to below-normal weather was expected in the Midwest and East through midmonth, though a slight warming trend was forecast for the weekend.

And while chart traders agreed the technical picture turned bullish after Friday's breakout and Monday's follow through, some said the market was overbought and due for a pullback after an 11 percent rise in four sessions.

September support was pegged at $2.20 and then at $2.15-2.16 and along the short-term up trendline at $2.125. Resistance was seen at the new contract high of $2.42 and at the May 7 spot continuation high of $2.43.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed eight cents to about the $2.30 level. Midcon pipes were up a dime to the mid-$2.20s. New York city gate prices gained a similar amount to about the $2.50 level.
NYMEX said 42,663 contracts traded at 1335 EDT.
On the KCBT, September firmed five cents to $2.27, while deferreds were steady to up eight cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.4 cents to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
